Subject: DPA & international transfer mechanics (Astoria / Redwood)

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the product demo last week — the team here is excited about the latency profile. Legal asked me to follow up on the data protection agreement and specifically how Redwood intends to cover international transfers for our UK and EU data subjects. A few items they want to confirm up front:

- Do you intend to execute a standard DPA + UK IDTA addendum, or to rely on SCCs only?
- Is there an option for Astoria to require the UK IDTA be executed in addition to the SCCs (we have UK-regulated customers)?
- We need an initial subprocessor list and any SOC2 evidence to accompany signing.

Elena (cc) will coordinate the redlines. Can you share an estimated timeline to get to an executed DPA + addendum via DocuSign? We are targeting a production start the week of Dec 6.

Appreciate it —
Tom
Tom Reyes
Head of Procurement, Astoria Financial

Tom / Elena —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front:
- We can sign a Redwood DPA plus the UK IDTA addendum (we treat that as our standard for UK data subjects).
- We also attach the EU SCCs as a fallback where customers prefer that mechanism; Redwood supports both and will include both in the envelope when requested.
- Subprocessor list: I’ll loop in Security to attach the current inventory and SOC 2 summary.

Timeline: if we receive redlines by EOD Monday 11/16, we can turn around internal review and send a DocuSign envelope with both the DPA and the UK addendum by Thursday 11/19, with a target signature date of 11/24. Does that align with your production target the week of 12/6?

Next steps I propose:
1) Elena sends redlines to this thread (track changes preferred).
2) Redwood legal (Neha) reviews and prepares clean + tracked versions.
3) Send combined envelope with DPA + UK IDTA + SCCs attachment (SCCs as incorporated terms) for signatures.

I’m cc’ing Neha and Aditya (security) so they can prep the attachments (SOC2 summary, subprocessor list, transfer impact note).

— Lauren Bishop
Director, Partnerships (Redwood Inference)

Lauren / Neha —

Attached are Astoria's redlines (Astoria_DPA_Redlines_v3.docx). Summary of the key asks:
- We have a mandatory clause that requires execution of the UK IDTA where the data subject is UK-based; please do not treat it as optional.
- Clarify the transfer impact assessment (section 6): we need a short summary of technical and organisational safeguards and an explicit reference that Redwood will rely on SCCs + UK addendum where necessary.
- Subprocessors: we need a commitment to notify prior to onboarding a subprocessor and a 30-day objection window; also request a named emergency contact for data incidents affecting transfers.

If you can confirm Redwood can accept those changes (or propose workable alternatives) we can move quickly.

Thanks —
Elena
Senior Counsel, Astoria Financial

Subject: RE: DPA & international transfer mechanics (Astoria / Redwood)

Elena —

Thanks for the redlines and the clear summary. We reviewed and here are Redwood’s positions on the main points: 

- UK IDTA: We can execute the UK IDTA as a required addendum for UK data subjects. Operationally we will include the UK IDTA as a separate document in the signing envelope and treat it as binding where applicable.

- Transfer Impact Assessment (TIA): We will provide a concise TIA summary (1–2 pages) that highlights our encryption in transit/at rest, access controls, key management, and international transfer safeguards. We’ll attach that as "transfer-impact-summary.pdf" in the envelope.

- Subprocessors: Redwood’s standard practice is to give notice of new subprocessors 30 days before onboarding and to accept a 30-day objection window. We cannot commit to named approval rights for every subprocessor but will commit to the notification + objection process and to providing an emergency escalation contact (security@redwood.com / +1-415-555-0123).

We are comfortable with Astoria’s proposed language with the following redlines: minor clarifications in liability cap application for transfer-related claims and explicit references to SCCs as a fallback where IDTA is not used. I’ve attached a clean and tracked package for your review.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
